trust_decision.summary: Whether HTTP clients reaching the public Caddy listener (or the container network) may talk to supervisord's XML-RPC/web admin interface; at the pinned commit Caddy forwards /supervisor/* to supervisord on 9001, which listens on all interfaces and is protected only by HTTP basic auth.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names the /supervisor Caddy route; this is the only place that route is defined.

fix_sites.entry_point: unknown: the supplied fix diff (fix.diff:1-2) is a release merge commit header with no hunks, so the changed source sites cannot be read

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who removes the Caddy /supervisor route could argue the direct supervisord listener on *:9001 is a container-internal port that is not published, so it is not part of 'the Caddy route' the report names.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The client links users to the supervisor log tail at /supervisor/logtail/backend, and supervisorctl, healthcheck and auto-heal scripts drive supervisord over the unix socket; removing the RPC interface or the unix socket breaks them.

O7_producer.where: deploy/docker/fs/opt/appsmith/caddy-reconfigure.mjs:41-217 generates the Caddyfile at runtime from a template string

O8_uncovered_routes.route: supervisord inet_http_server binds port 9001 on all interfaces, so it can be reached directly on the container network without going through Caddy
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The port is not published by default, and the report names only the Caddy route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file and different config layer (supervisord ini vs Caddy generator script)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Server-side datasource HTTP requests block loopback only when IN_DOCKER=1 and never block the container's own non-loopback address, so a datasource can reach supervisord on 9001 or the Caddy /supervisor path
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the general SSRF denylist, a neighbouring feature; self-hosted users legitimately query private-network APIs.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different language and package (Java server module vs Docker deploy scripts)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second server block (custom-domain HTTPS) that re-declares the supervisor proxy instead of importing all-config
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The generator already emits several site blocks; a maintainer adding a per-domain block could copy the route list.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an @backend-style path matcher that also lists a supervisor path alias
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Path matchers are grouped by lists here, so adding an alias is a one-word change.

O9_family: exposed admin interface / SSRF to internal service (CWE-183, CWE-918)

O10_build.language: Shell / JavaScript (Node .mjs) / supervisord ini; plus Java server for the SSRF denylist
O10_build.toolchain: Node for caddy-reconfigure.mjs; Caddy binary; Maven/JDK for app/server
O10_build.project_tests: No tests for caddy-reconfigure.mjs found under deploy/docker; WebClientUtils has app/server/appsmith-interfaces/src/test/java/com/appsmith/util/WebClientUtilsTest.java

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the redir/handle_path /supervisor lines in caddy-reconfigure.mjs and leave supervisord listening on *:9001.
